## Verdict

missing

## Bearer

WatchApp — app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/MainActivity.kt

## Trigger

Navigator moving to MAIN, PROJECTION, CONTROL or END, observed through
`navigator.current.collectAsStateWithLifecycle()` in `WatchApp` — observed.
A second, distinct occurrence of the same defect sits in
`PreparationScreen` (app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/preparation/PreparationScreen.kt),
triggered by its own `viewModel.uiState` collection when navigating to
PREPARATION — also observed, but through a different bearer that the
fix cannot avoid touching alongside `WatchApp`.

## Today

In `WatchApp` (MainActivity.kt:211-289), the `when (destination)` is
exhaustive on the eight `WatchDestination` values, but four of its
branches — MAIN, PROJECTION, CONTROL, END — each read one or two
`produceState<Race?>`/`produceState<Profile?>` values whose declared
initial value is `null`, then render only inside an `if (currentRace
!= null [&& profile != null])` with no `else`: while the
`produceState` block has not yet completed (or if `findInProgress()`
returns `Result.failure`, silently discarded by `.getOrNull()`, or
`profileRepository.observe().first()` never emits), the branch renders
nothing.

The PREPARATION branch does not use `produceState`; instead
`PreparationScreen.kt:31-32` collects `viewModel.uiState` (nullable
`PreparationUiState?`) and matches `null -> Unit`, rendering nothing
for as long as the view model's state has not produced a first value.

In both cases nothing distinguishes "still resolving" from "resolution
failed": the same absent rendering covers both, and no error is ever
shown to the user.

## Expected

Each of the five destinations (PREPARATION, MAIN, PROJECTION, CONTROL,
END) renders a loading state while its data is resolving and a
distinct error state if the read fails, per R88 — never nothing. This
requires two bearers, not one: `WatchApp`'s four `produceState`-driven
branches need their own loading/error floor instead of `if` without
`else`, and `PreparationScreen`'s `null` branch needs the same
distinction instead of `null -> Unit`. A second gap the fix must also
close: today `findInProgress()`'s `Result.failure` is discarded through
`.getOrNull()` in the three `produceState` blocks that call it (MAIN,
PROJECTION, CONTROL), so a source failure currently reads as "not
started yet" — the same absence `produceState`'s own `null` initial
value already produces; carrying the failure through requires reading
the `Result` itself rather than `.getOrNull()`, so the new error state
can be reached.
